in_hebrew.name: טימותיאה
in_hebrew.long_meaning: טימותיאה נגזר מהמילים היווניות 'טימוס' (כבוד) ו'תאוס' (אלוהים). המשמעות היא 'מכובדת לאלוהים' או 'מורא אלוהים'. השם קשור לנושא של כבוד ויראת אלוהים בלב הנוצרי.

in_greek.name: Τιμοτέα
in_greek.long_meaning: Το όνομα Τιμοτέα προέρχεται από τις ελληνικές λέξεις 'τίμη' (τιμή) και 'Θεός' (Θεός). Σημαίνει 'τιμή προς τον Θεό' ή 'φόβος του Θεού'. Στην παράδοση της Εκκλησίας, το όνομα αυτό συμβολίζει την τιμή και την υπακοή προς τον Θεό.

in_latin.name: Timotea

In the Christian tradition, Timotea symbolizes piety, devotion, and reverence to God. Historically, the name is associated with spiritual values and moral integrity. The name is used across various Christian cultures, signifying a connection to faith and divine respect.

historical_references.reference: In the New Testament of the Bible, there are two characters named Timothy, but one of them is commonly referred to as Timotea in Romance languages. This Timothy was a disciple of the apostle Paul and was sent on missionary journeys with him. He was a native of Lystra in Lycaonia, in Asia Minor, and was converted to Christianity by Paul. This event occurred around 49-52 AD.
historical_references.context: New Testament, Apostle Paul's missionary journeys

historical_references.reference: During the Middle Ages in Europe, a legend grew up around Timothy of Lystra, who was believed to have been a priest in the early Christian church. He was said to have suffered martyrdom during the persecution of Christians under the Roman Emperor Decius, around 249-251 AD. This legend contributed to the popularization of the name Timotea among Christians in Romance-speaking regions.
